scenes.card: Built during the event. A research tool, not medical advice.
scenes.vo: Everything you are about to see was built during this event. It is a research tool, not medical advice. This is a pharmacogenomic lab report from India, travelling the way these reports really travel: a photograph on WhatsApp.

scenes.card: India's evidence base: two studies, about 3,600 people.
scenes.vo: India's published evidence on these gene variants rests on about two studies and three and a half thousand people. Thousands of reports like this one are issued every year, and not one of them reaches a dataset.
Muse Spark reads the photograph under a strict schema. It quotes every gene call directly from the page, and records which variants the laboratory says it actually tested.

scenes.card: PharmCAT standardises. Deterministic rules check coverage.
scenes.vo: PharmCAT, the reference engine behind the CPIC guidelines, standardises the allele names. Our own rules then check which India-relevant variants this panel never tested, and the patient reference is stripped before anything is stored.

scenes.card: The same photograph, on open weights.
scenes.vo: Here is the same report read again by Muse Spark Open. Open weights mean a biobank can run this entirely inside its own network, which is the only version of this that could ever touch a real patient's report.

scenes.card: Muse Voice. Malayalam and English, mixed.
scenes.vo: Muse Voice takes results read aloud, Malayalam and English mixed together the way people actually speak in a Kochi clinic, and Muse Spark reads that transcript into the very same record.

scenes.card: A human curator signs off every call.
scenes.vo: A curator checks each call against the quoted source before it counts. Muse Spark web search pulls what has been published for India, with the sources attached.

scenes.card: Carrier frequencies. Wilson intervals. One CSV.
scenes.vo: Every reviewed record joins a cohort. Carrier frequencies with confidence intervals, honest denominators, and one download that is ready for a study.

We did not grade ourselves on our own fixtures. We ran it against two public sources of truth: the CDC's reference materials programme, and real thirty-x genomes from the Thousand Genomes Project. Two hundred and eight real human samples. Six hundred and twenty-two of six hundred and forty-six gene calls agree with the laboratory consensus. Every single mismatch is traced and written down.

scenes.card: The benchmark argued our own case.
scenes.vo: And the benchmark made our argument for us. Six disagreements were decreased-function alleles that the consensus panel simply never looked for. All six were African-ancestry samples. A panel designed somewhere else, calling a carrier a non-carrier.

Because reading the report is the easy half. We simulated a hundred and twenty Indian people, each with a report from a laboratory that tests only part of the panel. Counting a panel that never tested c.85T>C as a non-carrier puts the frequency at fifteen percent. The truth was twenty-five. A ten point error, downward, on the variant a quarter of Indians carry.
Pathya. Research data, from the reports India already has.
